dimension_justifications.soundness: The ownership contract, storage-interval predicate, factorial controls, and denominator distinctions are unusually explicit. However, the main semantic comparisons are same-backend relational checks, while the independent numerical checks cover only eight attention rows and four post-normalization GDN transitions (pp. 8, 18-19). Moreover, the manuscript explicitly concedes that the replayable captured evidence cannot establish correctness before capture (p. 19), and the original GPU code closure failed (p. 9). These are substantive limits for a paper whose central contribution is an executable correctness audit.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Excellent. The paper is highly readable, carefully scoped, and unusually clear about the distinction between logical state, allocator counters, process memory, and service capacity (pp. 7-9). Figures and tables are legible, claims are paired with boundaries, and the appendices make the protocol concrete.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The integration of heterogeneous-state ownership witnesses, phase-aware accounting, and fault-gated replay is useful engineering methodology. Still, the paper itself positions all individual ingredients as established and demonstrates the integration on one fixed stack, one schedule, and a narrow set of operator samples (pp. 17-19). Its general research contribution is therefore presently incremental and insufficiently validated beyond that reference case.

paper_summary: ForkAudit proposes an executable audit protocol for sharing a long document prefix among hybrid LLM continuations, separating token-indexed attention KV ownership from mutable GDN recurrent state. It evaluates four full-copy/shared-document KV by materialized/borrowed-GDN setup cells on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, reports identical recorded tokens, canonical logit/state digests, range-based ownership witnesses, sampled independent attention and GDN oracles, targeted fault-gate outcomes, and allocator deltas. The paper appropriately limits its claims to one reference stack and explicitly disclaims throughput, scheduler, capacity, and broad production claims.
strongest_verified_contribution: A clear, phase-aware specification of what a bounded hybrid-state ownership audit should record and distinguish: immutable document KV/base state, private append/rebound state, callable and append contracts, storage-range witnesses, and explicitly named memory denominators (Sections 3-4, pp. 4-7).
strengths: The central distinction between token-indexed KV sharing and recurrent-state rebinding is technically well motivated and clearly specified (pp. 1-5).
The paper does not conflate logical payload, page allocation, PyTorch allocator counters, NVML memory, and admitted service capacity (p. 7; Table 2 on p. 9; Table 6 on p. 16).

The scope statements are unusually candid: sequential single-stream execution, one model/runtime/geometry, targeted positive controls, and selected captured-input oracle boundaries are all disclosed (pp. 2, 8-9, 19).
The pointer-free interval formulation and lifecycle conditions make the claimed ownership predicate more auditable than token equality alone (Appendix D, pp. 14-15).
questions: How can an independent reviewer establish that two distinct producer-assigned storage IDs do not denote the same underlying allocation, given that absolute addresses are prohibited and the paper admits the captured records are not proof against a malicious or faulty pre-capture producer (Appendix D, pp. 14-15; Appendix I, p. 19)?

Will the authors provide a fully closed, independently rerunnable GPU execution artifact rather than only a derivative replay package, given the stated terminal recursive code-closure failure (Section 7, p. 9)?

Can the authors add an independent end-to-end reference on a representative subset, or at minimum broaden the attention/GDN sampling across layers, requests, positions, and lengths, to bound common-mode errors that cross-arm digest equality cannot expose (Section 5.2-5.3, p. 8)?

Why should one hand-selected targeted mutation per listed failure mode be considered sufficient evidence that the proposed gates are useful beyond intended-gate reachability, particularly when M8 reaches only an injected sentinel (Appendix F and H, pp. 16, 18-19)?

issues.location: Submitted PDF artifact identity; related central frozen-identity target in Section 3, p. 4, and reproducibility statement, p. 9
issues.observed_evidence: The PDF at the supplied path hashes to 73f8628ae23119c6c964e5d86670c5c193162a36d22d320d478e249d74126683, which does not match the mandated frozen snapshot SHA-256 802c99cf2ec462e41b5343dd204c463b3f4d27d0eb3c601e6489d2765e1e7a27. This conflicts with the paper's frozen-identity premise, whose mandatory records are specified on p. 4.
issues.why_it_matters: A review of a different binary cannot validate claims assigned to the declared frozen snapshot. For this manuscript, artifact identity is also a central methodological requirement rather than incidental metadata.
issues.required_fix: Resolve the artifact-identity discrepancy before evaluation: publish the intended PDF under the declared hash, or update the frozen manifest and all review metadata to the actual PDF hash with a documented immutable release record.
issues.verification_test: Independently compute SHA-256 from the released PDF and require exact equality with the submission manifest, review metadata, and artifact index before any replay or score aggregation.
issues.evidence_needed: A single immutable release manifest binding the reviewed PDF, code, raw receipts, and replay package to consistent hashes.

issues.location: Section 3 decision rule, p. 4; Section 7, p. 9; Appendix I, p. 19
issues.observed_evidence: The paper declares targets fully witnessed if records and a replay predicate exist (p. 4), but later states that terminal recursive closure of the primary GPU code failed and that the derivative package binds a raw aggregate and offline replay rather than a closed original run (p. 9). It also states that pointer-free intervals and hashes are replayable evidence, not proof against a malicious producer before capture (p. 19).
issues.why_it_matters: Recomputing predicates from producer-generated receipts establishes internal consistency, not that the captured state faithfully represents the executed runtime. This leaves the principal ownership-correctness claim dependent on an unstated trust assumption and weakens the meaning of the reported 'full' target status.
issues.required_fix: State a formal producer/trust model and downgrade the relevant guarantee to conditional if independent capture cannot be supplied. Preferably release a fully pinned GPU execution environment and an independently rerunnable collection path that binds runtime allocation identity and capture events before aggregation.
issues.verification_test: A clean independent execution must reproduce the raw receipt set and aggregate; adversarial tests must attempt forged storage-ID relabeling and pre-capture aliasing while preserving reported hashes, and the verifier or trusted capture layer must reject them.
issues.evidence_needed: A complete execution closure, an independent rerun, and evidence that the capture mechanism detects aliasing or relabeling not visible to the current receipt schema.

issues.location: Section 5.1-5.3, pp. 7-8; Table 5, p. 14; Appendix I, p. 19
issues.observed_evidence: The four ownership cells are compared using identical-backend canonical digests, so common-mode errors can agree. The independent attention check covers eight selected rows conditional on captured post-RoPE inputs (p. 8), and the GDN oracle covers four transitions at layers 0, 10, 20, and 38 conditional on post-native-normalization inputs (pp. 8, 18). The manuscript explicitly excludes upstream construction, normalization, most GDN layers, and end-to-end behavior (pp. 8, 19).
issues.why_it_matters: The sampled operator checks are valuable but cannot validate the central implementation's end-to-end correctness or rule out a shared implementation error across the ownership arms. The current evidence supports a bounded consistency audit, not a broadly sound hybrid-state correctness result.
issues.required_fix: Narrow the headline and target-status wording to conditional consistency unless broader validation is added. Add an independently implemented end-to-end baseline for a representative subset and stratified oracle samples across attention layers, GDN layers, requests, decoding positions, and prefix-tail geometries.
issues.verification_test: Pre-register a coverage plan; report per-stratum errors and failures against an independent end-to-end implementation or a separately validated backend, including cases designed to induce upstream normalization/projection and append-path errors.
issues.evidence_needed: Independent end-to-end comparisons plus wider, pre-specified operator coverage showing that the sampled checks generalize within the stated reference stack.

issues.location: Section 5.3, p. 8; Table 7, p. 16; Appendix H, pp. 18-19
issues.observed_evidence: The nine mutants are targeted positive controls with one intended gate each. The paper explicitly says this is intended-gate reachability rather than completeness or a detector rate (p. 8); after suppression, M9 reaches one ordinary assertion but M8 reaches only an injected sentinel, and both abort before semantic outputs are observed (pp. 18-19).
issues.why_it_matters: The central empirical validation of gate sensitivity mostly demonstrates that handcrafted checks fire on faults constructed for those checks. It does not establish useful coverage of plausible unanticipated faults, false-negative behavior, or whether errors reach observable semantic consequences.
issues.required_fix: Report the result as nine targeted positive-control demonstrations, not general fault sensitivity. Add a mutation matrix with multiple independent fault implementations per target, wrong-gate/false-positive controls, escaped-fault accounting, and downstream-output checks when safe.
issues.verification_test: Freeze a fault corpus before execution and report a confusion matrix over intended gates, observed gates, clean controls, wrong-gate cases, escapes, and semantic divergences.
issues.evidence_needed: A broader preregistered mutation campaign with nontrivial faults not mechanically coupled to the tested assertion.

issues.observed_evidence: Table 2 reports rounded medians over eight ranks while stating rank values coincide; Table 6 likewise says values were identical across all ranks. The PDF provides neither unrounded rank endpoints nor an explicit receipt-derived equality listing.
issues.why_it_matters: This does not invalidate the carefully bounded allocator claim, but the median framing obscures whether equality is exact, rounded equality, or an aggregate assertion. Since memory accounting is a main quantitative outcome, the presentation should permit direct checking.
issues.required_fix: Provide unrounded per-rank allocator endpoints and the exact baseline/reset definitions in the main artifact summary, or state that the table reports one deterministic endpoint with a receipt hash proving identical values.
issues.verification_test: Recompute Table 2 and Table 6 from raw synchronized allocator snapshots and verify the displayed values, rank equality claim, units, and reset boundaries.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-rank raw allocator snapshots or a machine-readable table with exact byte values and aggregation code.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, or safety issue is apparent from this systems evaluation. The manuscript includes an appropriately limited ethics statement on p. 13.
llm_usage_disclosure: This internal review was produced with LLM assistance. It was based only on the supplied PDF, review rubric, and schema; not verified code.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: Resolution of the PDF snapshot-hash mismatch with one immutable, internally consistent release manifest.
A fully closed and independently rerunnable GPU execution/capture artifact, accompanied by an explicit trust model for storage and receipt capture.
Pre-specified independent end-to-end validation on representative cases and broader stratified attention/GDN oracle coverage.
A broader mutation campaign showing wrong-gate behavior, clean-control false-positive behavior, escapes, and downstream semantic consequences.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Confirmation that the submitted PDF is not the declared frozen snapshot or that no immutable artifact identity can be established.
Failure to independently rerun the reported receipt collection or discovery that storage identities can be relabeled/forged without rejection.
Any independent end-to-end comparison revealing semantic divergence despite the reported cross-arm digest matches.
Evidence that the nine fault outcomes depend solely on injected sentinels or assertions without detecting corresponding runtime defects.
review_limitations: This was a PDF-only blind review. I did not inspect code, raw receipts, supplementary artifacts, prior reviews, or revision history.
The score evaluates the evidence and claims available in the supplied manuscript, not an artifact replay.
